title: EMBRACE: Shaping Inclusive Opinion Representation by Aligning Implicit Conversations with Social Norms
findings: The paper uses examples of anti-Muslim sentiment ('Muslim terrorists') and implicit toxicity ('Make a joke on prophet') as part of its dataset for evaluating normative alignment. The findings are not broken down specifically by religion, but generally show that LLMs have a higher likelihood of agreeing with explicit harmful opinions compared to human experts, and respond with more neutrality to implicit harmful opinions, indicating a failure to consistently adopt a normatively-aligned oppositional stance against toxic content, including religiously-targeted hate.

measurement_description: The benchmark measured model stance alignment with social norms when presented with implicit and explicit toxic statements. This included evaluating responses to harmful content related to religious groups and figures, such as anti-Muslim rhetoric and jokes about prophets, to assess whether the model would appropriately disagree.
